newsitem.title: USA: Greenpeace to cut U.S. staff, close offices.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace to cut U.S. staff, close offices.

text.p: Greenpeace, the environmental activist group, said Wednesday it will be cutting its U.S. staff to 65 from about 400 and closing its regional offices in the wake of declining membership in recent years.
"We are going to be consolidating most of our efforts into the Washington D.C. headquarters and we will be closing 11 field offices," said Greenpeace spokeswoman Deborah Rephan.

Most of the layoffs come from Greenpeace's decision to discontinue its door-to-door canvass, which has been the mainstay of its efforts to raise money, gain new members, collect petition signatures and other activities.

"Membership has declined over the last several years and that means less money coming in. (The canvass) has been a very important part our activities but it was an increasingly expensive way to operate and not the best way to spend our donors' resources," Rephan said.
The decision to cut back followed several year of debate within the organization which forced a "radical rethink" of Greenpeace's efforts in order to avoid "financial disaster," said Rephan.

Despite closing all but the Washington D.C. office, she said Greenpeace would continue to persue local and regional campaigns through its activists throughout the country, though they will be working from home in the future.
The cuts become effective at the end of August, Rephan said.
